text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Newspaper editorial says ruling Democratic Party founder Azem Hajdari has lost his chance of a greater role in politics after President Sali Berisha chose to support the existing leader of the independent trade union against him in a contest for the union's presidency.
- Prosecutors are looking into past trials of appeals court chief judge Prel Martini to try to discover a motive for an attack that wrecked his apartment on Wednesday night.

- Two small parties, centre-right Democratic Alliance and the centre-left Social Democrats, say a Constitutional Assembly should convene in January to draw up a constitution and then hold a referendum on the issue.

- Albanians continue to put their lek savings into high interest pyramid schemes offered by local firms, boosting the value of the lek against the dollar. If the government does not intervene the dollar could sink to 80 leks from more than 100.
- Albanian police have busted a drug ring, arresting four people distributing drugs in Albania, Macedonia and Germany.
- As the fifth anti-genocide trial continues, the supreme court will try 11 ex-senior communists at the end of November.
- Police have arrested the brother of Klement Kolaneci, late communist dictator Enver Hoxha's son-in-law. Both are suspected of having links with an alleged guerrilla group.
- More than 300 illegal Albanian emigrants have been stopped by Italian police in the Puglia region.
- Police have found a truck carrying some $40,000 worth of cigarettes in northern Albania, smuggled from Yugoslavia.
- Independent newspapers are proving more popular on the Albanian market than the political party media.
- Two young Albanian girls were knifed to death in Italy.
- Police discovered an arsenal of arms in the northern highland region of Mirdite.
- Parliament passed a decree making privatisation vouchers valid until the end of 1999.
- Authorities have promised inhabitants of a building wrecked by an explosion on Wednesday that they will be able to move back in within a month.
